message:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?
response:
## Van name ideas
- **Veneer Diesel**
- **Dovetail**
- **Chester Drawers**
- **French Polish**
- **The Restoration Wagon**

Veneer Diesel probably wins the staff vote.

## Tomorrow's route: B → A → C

This is the only order that works. B must be finished before 09:30, which rules out going to A first. C can't take anything before 11:00, so it has to be last.

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 – 09:05 | **Drop B**: unload (finished 25 min before opening) |
| 09:05 – 09:30 | Drive B → A |
| 09:30 – 09:45 | **Drop A**: unload (inside 09:00–10:00 window) |
| 09:45 – 10:25 | Drive A → C |
| 10:25 – 10:55 | **Break**: taken near C while waiting |
| 11:00 – 11:15 | **Drop C**: unload |
| 11:15 – 12:00 | Drive C → depot |
| **12:00** | **Back at depot** |

**The return has no slack.** The earliest C can be unloaded is 11:00–11:15, and the drive back takes 45 minutes, so 12:00 is the earliest possible return whatever the order. Any hold-up at C, or traffic on the way back, makes him late. Before tomorrow, I'd do one of these:
- confirm the driver can be unloading at C at 11:00 sharp;
- ask C whether they can accept at 10:45; or
- check whether the 12:00 return can stretch a little.

The morning has some room. He could leave as late as about 08:55 and still finish B before 09:30.

## "On the way" text
> Hi [Name], it's [Driver] from [Company]. I'm on my way with your furniture and should be with you in about [X] minutes. See you soon!

## Three handover checks
1. **No new damage.** Compare against the condition at loading: scratches, dents, chips, scuffs or marks on upholstery.
2. **Everything works and is complete.** Drawers and doors run smoothly, handles and hardware are tight, legs are secure, and any loose parts and keys are handed over.
3. **It's the right item.** It matches the order and the customer is happy with it before signing.

## Paper or emailed delivery note?
Email by default. It can't get lost, it's searchable, and the customer can sign on the driver's phone. Keep printed copies for customers who prefer paper, and for businesses that need one for their records.

## Proof of delivery (for the part-timer)
"Proof of delivery is the record showing an item was handed over: usually the customer's signature and name, the time, and a photo of the item in place."

## Evening-before text
> Hi [Name], [Company] here. Your furniture is due tomorrow between [9:00] and [10:00]. We'll text when the driver's on the way. Reply to rearrange.

The fixed wording is about 125 characters, which leaves around 35 for the customer's name and your company name.

**Two things that stop it splitting into two messages:**
- **No emoji, and only straight apostrophes (').** Curly apostrophes (') and emoji switch the message to a format with a 70-character limit. Many phones insert curly apostrophes automatically.
- **Only include "Reply to rearrange" if someone monitors that number.**
